# Historical pre-fit readiness dossier — 2026-10-17

Historical status at intake: preparation only; no GO/NO-GO decision has been made. This is not
SPEC-029/T008 completion. A registered public-source intake audit has been run;
no rows are admitted for fitting or accepted test evaluation.

The owner's product direction and zero external-spend limit are recorded in
[the native delivery revision](../../specs/030-system-one-model/native-delivery.md).
Sources/labels and a finite local execution envelope must be reviewed before
fitting. Existing [evaluation policy](../../specs/029-system-one-evaluation/evaluation-protocol.md)
continues to govern grouped 60/15/10/15 splits, calibration/threshold separation,
blind adjudication, feasibility floors, risk/coverage and paired complete costs.

| Candidate | Observed source condition | Current disposition |
|---|---|---|
| microsoft/Multilingual-MiniLM-L12-H384 | Metadata declares MIT; no safetensors or standalone license file listed | Do not load pickle; require another verified artifact or reviewed safe conversion route |
| sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 | Metadata declares Apache-2.0 and lists model.safetensors; no standalone license file listed | Preferred encoder candidate for further rights/tokenizer review, not admitted |
| Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B | Metadata declares Apache-2.0; LICENSE and safetensors listed | Future causal comparator; outside this cut's tested family/parameter envelope |

Exact revisions and metadata hashes are in the source manifest. Metadata tags
are evidence to inspect, not a substitute for an actual rights decision. No model
weights have been downloaded. No speed or quality ranking has been established.

The software packet supports finite synthetic optimization/export and all three
typed readouts. Those controls cannot furnish independent human labels, real-source
yield, deployment economics or a positive utility finding. Leave original
SPEC-029/030 research tasks pending until their actual evidence exists.

## Public corpus candidates and bounded intake audit

`AmazonScience/massive` declares CC-BY-4.0 in retrieved metadata and is a candidate
for intent/choice transfer tests. `facebook/xnli` has no license value in its
retrieved metadata; rights remain unresolved. Exact revisions and metadata hashes
are in source-register.json. XNLI remains metadata-only. MASSIVE 1.1 was captured
for an audit under its published CC-BY-4.0 terms, with registration before
retrieval and explicit byte/time limits. This does not approve model fitting.
Neither source supplies evidence about Braid effect correctness or commutation.
Intent/NLI coverage cannot replace ordinal, internal-workflow or blind adjudicated
test coverage. Both retain source/label/feasibility review before fitting or adoption.

The [aggregate audit](../../specs/030-system-one-model/evidence/public-source-audit.json)
binds the 40,251,390-byte archive to SHA-256
`4cba5faa11c71437928e17cb1b9b3d8b8e727e7ea363a3a9a8045e19c0491577`.
Only en-US/es-ES JSONL members were parsed; raw data stays outside the repository.
The [registration](../../specs/030-system-one-model/evidence/public-source-registration.json)
and [offline reproducer](../../specs/030-system-one-model/evidence/audit-public-source.py)
separate intake permission from training/adoption decisions.

| 16,521 rows per locale, 33,042 total; 18 scenarios and 60 intents per locale | Scenario choice fits the 32-option profile; 60-intent questions require a separate approved narrowing strategy |
| English has no source-provided quality judgments | Cannot claim EN ordinal coverage or complete blind labeling from this source |

## Later local studies — 2026-10-18

The separate owner-authorized [local pilot](local_pilot/report.md) subsequently
admitted the pinned MASSIVE source taxonomy and safe encoder for bounded local
research. Its two exact preregistrations, Luna pre-fit reviews, real fits, separate

The statements above describe the earlier intake boundary; they do not deny those

# Partial encoder adaptation pilot, version 2

Registered after observing version 1's frozen-encoder test failure in 18-way choice,
before any version 2 optimization or test predictions. This is an adaptive second
study, not a preregistered extension of version 1 or replication of its exact test.
The owner authorizes continued real local EN/ES training/calibration/evaluation on
M3 Pro, EUR0 external. The same narrow source admission, attribution, taxonomy proxy
rubric, no-network execution and no-promotion boundaries apply. Human general
workflow adequacy, independent blind labels and Laya parity remain unestablished.

Select the next 4,000 lowest `pilot-v1:sample` hash components after excluding every
component selected for version 1. Recompute components over the same pinned complete
source with the identical grouping algorithm. No original ID, aligned translation
or detected duplicate component may occur in both studies. Use unchanged 60/15/10/15
hash allocation and typed questions; freeze actual counts and semantic classes
before fitting. The new test is untouched by version 1 and never passed to fitting,
calibration, threshold selection or hyperparameter selection. Shared base pretraining
or undetected paraphrases remain contamination limitations. Do not silently pool
results from the two studies.

Candidate: native EncoderScorer, headLayers=0, same licensed pretrained base. Freeze
embeddings and the first 10 BERT layers; train the final 2 layers plus owned type
embedding and scorer. Three seeds17/29/43, primary17 predeclared. Shuffle seed order
with Python Random(20261019).shuffle([17,29,43]). Train exactly3 epochs, batch16,
AdamW backbone lr2e-5, head lr1e-3, clip global gradient norm1. Keep frozen layers in
eval mode, trainable last layers in train mode during fitting, and all layers in
eval mode for measurement. No validation-driven stopping or test tuning. Inputs
retain full production rendering with maximum512 tokens and no truncation.

References: version1's fixed primary-seed head and linear scorer evaluated on the
new test, plus version2 train-majority. They were trained on different groups; these
are transfer references, not a controlled causal ablation or matched training-data
comparison. Their temperatures/thresholds may be refitted using only version2's
calibration/threshold partitions. Do not claim matched-chain speedup from this study.
No unavailable decoder/System2/advisor baseline is counted as zero.

Calibration and policy: unchanged fixed temperature grid and separate confidence
threshold grid from protocol.md, >=200 calibration examples with every semantic
class represented, >=50 threshold accepted examples and empirical error<=5%. Sparse
strata abstain. Check semantic scenario identity rather than shuffled option position.
These policy estimates are descriptive, not the one-sided precision promotion gate.
Report all seeds, raw/calibrated NLL/Brier/ECE, accuracy/macro recall/confusion,
expected-score MAE and modal ordinal MAE, risk/coverage, accepted counts/errors and
cluster descriptive intervals, paired bootstrap versus transfer references and
majority (10,000 seed20261018), missingness and all actual denominators.

CPU6 float32, no MPS, no paid service; <=20min perseed, <=45min for this adaptation
execution, <=16GiB RSS and <=8GiB task disk. Retain the original pilot's 3h total
wall deadline, including earlier preprocessing/fitting and restarts; do not reset it.
Stop on budget/integrity/leakage failure; a negative result is valid. Export only
primary17 as experimental with correct source/license attribution, calibrated
research sidecar bound separately, no official catalogue or strict promotion.
Measure loading and complete warm render/tokenize/infer/calibration/readout costs
only after fitting and policy freeze, with competing local validation paused. Cold
means newly loaded object; OS filesystem caches are uncontrolled. Energy, fallback,
verifier, execution effects and external model costs remain unmeasured/unavailable.

Independent review must bind exact version2 code, source/tokenized split hashes,
yields, seed order, hardware and budget before fitting. Keep version1 evidence and
its negative result unchanged. Required engineering validation runs once on the
stable final code; interrupted earlier profiles do not count as passed.

# Local MASSIVE taxonomy-transfer pilot, version 1

Registered 2026-10-18 before fitting or test predictions. Scope: a narrow,
source-annotated taxonomy-transfer experiment on the owner's Apple M3 Pro (36 GiB).
Owner direction: actual local EN/ES training, calibration and evaluation, external
spend EUR 0. This document does not amend SPEC-029 or authorize promotion.

## Claim and rights

MASSIVE 1.1 archive SHA-256
`4cba5faa11c71437928e17cb1b9b3d8b8e727e7ea363a3a9a8045e19c0491577`
contains public utterances, scenario and intent annotations. Local research processing
uses the publisher's CC-BY-4.0 declaration and archive NOTICE (SLURP attribution).
Retain raw inputs, private split manifests, features and weights only under ignored
`artifacts/system-one/local-pilot/`; commit aggregate results, code and provenance.
Retain until explicit project cleanup. Do not publish raw text, worker identities or
weights. No private sessions, teacher API, external evaluation service or paid compute.

Base: sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2, revision
`e8f8c211226b894fcb81acc59f3b34ba3efd5f42`. Publisher card declares Apache-2.0;
retain the pinned card, license text and attribution. Download only pinned config,
fast tokenizer JSON and safetensors; validate sizes and SHA-256. No remote code or
pickle. Absence of a standalone upstream LICENSE remains a distribution-review
limitation; local processing is based on the publisher's declaration, not legal advice.

This pilot admits source-provided taxonomy labels only, not new independently
adjudicated human labels. It cannot establish general decision quality, agent-workflow
utility, semantic safety, grammar assessment or parity with Laya. SPEC-029's two blind
reviewers, real workflow outcomes and promotion gates remain pending. STSB multi-MT,
SemRel and SST5 are not admitted: fragmented or missing rights, commercial restrictions
or withheld test targets prevent treating them as freely reusable ordinal evidence.

## Units, grouping and labels

Read all 16,521 original IDs in each of en-US/es-ES. Join translations by ID and
normalize text (Unicode NFKC, case-fold, whitespace/punctuation). Union exact matches
across IDs and languages. Also union token sets with Jaccard >= .9 detected through
identical sets or one-token-deletion signatures (at least 10 tokens). This bounded
near-duplicate heuristic does not establish absence of semantic paraphrases or base
pretraining contamination. Group before sampling or partitioning; all derivatives
of one component remain together. Audit conflicts without silently removing them.

Select the 4,000 components with lowest SHA-256 of `pilot-v1:sample:<group>`.
Partition by SHA-256 `pilot-v1:split:<group>` into train 60%, calibration 15%,
threshold 10%, test 15%. Freeze hashes and actual counts before fitting. Official
partitions are deliberately regrouped because the audit found cross-partition text
matches. Do not describe this as an official MASSIVE benchmark score.

Each real utterance yields three questions with no generated utterance or teacher:
- Choice: its annotated scenario among all 18 scenarios, supplied descriptions in
  the utterance's language, with deterministic per-ID option permutation.
- Boolean: whether it belongs to a supplied scenario. Hash chooses positive or
  negative with equal probability; negatives choose a different scenario.
- Score: taxonomy match to a supplied intent: 0 different scenario, 1 same scenario
  but different intent, 2 matching intent. Hash chooses a desired level uniformly;
  if same-scenario alternatives do not exist, level 1 falls back to 0 and is counted.
  These derived ordinal targets are a taxonomy proxy, not human quality judgments.

Descriptions and rubric are frozen before features/fitting. Exclude only malformed
rows or complete rendered questions exceeding 512 tokens; report counts by split,
language and type. No truncation. Calibration eligibility requires >=200 examples
and each target class per language/type; ineligible groups remain uncalibrated and
cannot produce accepted-policy results. Test labels are never passed to optimizers,
calibration or threshold selection. Test scoring occurs once after all seeds and
policies are frozen; implementation failures may restart only with explicit logs.

## Candidates and budget

Primary seed 17 fixed in advance; also report seeds 29 and 43 without selecting a
winner on test.
The six (family, seed) runs start from family order [linear, native] and seeds
[17, 29, 43], then use Python Random(20261018).shuffle; freeze the resulting order.
Frozen CPU float32 BERT; native EncoderScorer with headLayers=0; train only type
embedding and scorer. Cache the exact contextual marker states from
production rendering. Verify cached logits equal full forward and backbone unchanged.
Train each seed 30 epochs, AdamW lr .001, batch 128, clip norm 1; no early stopping,
validation-driven hyperparameters or test selection. Compare against initial random
head, train-majority and a train-only linear scorer over the same frozen features.
Linear candidate uses the same epochs/seeds/batches/lr and calibration treatment.
Other SPEC-029 baselines, decoder pointer and System 2 remain unavailable in this
study; do not enter them as zero performance. No Laya/Jev installation or checkpoint.

CPU threads 6, feature batch 16, maximum 512 tokens, no MPS/GPU. Hard limits: total
execution 3 hours, feature extraction 90 minutes, each fit 20 minutes, RSS 16 GiB,
download 600 MiB, task disk 8 GiB; stop on leakage, changed hashes, rights failure or
budget exhaustion. A pre-fit throughput smoke may inspect training inputs only;
if this budget cannot finish the fixed sample, stop and register a new version
before fitting. Report actual wall time and RSS; energy is unmeasured.

## Calibration, policy and analysis

Fit one scalar temperature per seed/candidate/language/type on calibration only,
minimizing NLL over a fixed grid [0.25, 0.35, 0.5, 0.7, 1, 1.4, 2, 3, 5, 8].
Choose a confidence threshold on the separate threshold split: grid .50 through .99
in .01 increments; maximize coverage subject to >=50 accepted items and empirical
error <=.05, ties choose higher threshold. If none qualifies, always abstain.
This is descriptive policy fitting, not the reviewed confidence-bound promotion rule.

Report per-language/type counts, class counts, accuracy, macro recall and confusion,
NLL, multiclass Brier, 10 fixed-bin top-label ECE, expected-score MAE and separately
modal ordinal-class MAE, raw/calibrated results,
coverage, accepted error and group counts. Report paired group bootstrap accuracy
differences (10,000 resamples, seed 20261018), with descriptive intervals only: the
proxy labels and contamination uncertainty prevent broad scientific utility claims.
Include risk-coverage points and unavailable/missing denominators. Measure real CPU
cold model loading plus render/tokenize/inference/policy and warm complete inference
on preselected test examples only after policy freeze, including feature cache costs
separately. No fallback/verifier/execution exists in this pilot, so those costs are
unavailable, not free System 2 equivalence. Record no execution authorization.

Keep exported models experimental and product calibrationStatus absent; research
calibration is a separate hash-bound sidecar and does not silently enable strict
production decisions. Negative/inconclusive outcomes are valid. Independent review
must assess this narrower scope and implementation before fitting. Human source,
workflow acceptance, clean candidate freeze and artifact distribution remain pending.

## Exploratory follow-up after opening the test

A post-hoc original-base mean-pooled prototype diagnostic, with no fitting or policy tuning, scored 53.58/45.77% EN/ES scenario accuracy using the frozen 18 scenario descriptions, and 69.71/56.51% using the 60 intent descriptions mapped to scenarios. Both variants are reported. These results use the already-opened adaptation test: they are exploratory, not a fresh primary comparison or promotion evidence. They suggest useful semantic information in the base while the present marker head fails to discriminate choices; they do not isolate a causal explanation.

The next research candidate should compare pooled semantic representations against the deeper Laya-derived marker head using matched training data, fixed optimization budgets and a new unopened holdout. More epochs on these opened tests would not establish generalization. Real Braid workflow utility still requires an authorized workflow corpus and independent blind labels.

See [the next comparison design](next-comparison.md) for the bounded matched-data experiment and separate workflow track.

# Preregistered matched-data choice representation comparison

Status: prospective local research; fitting requires the exact registration and
an actual independent Luna pre-fit assessment. Owner direction: continue the
semantic/Laya-head comparison with common data and a new holdout on Apple M3 Pro,
with EUR 0 external spend, and implement improved option selection. This does not
admit general workflows, human quality labels, distribution or promotion.

Use the previously pinned MASSIVE 1.1 EN/ES archive and multilingual MiniLM safe
base under the separately recorded local source admission. No network, source
acquisition, Laya/Jev package or upstream decision checkpoint. Exclude every
aligned/exact/near-duplicate component from both completed 4,000-component studies.
Select the next 4,000 by the original prospective sample hash, without looking at
model predictions. A new salted group hash `choice-v1:split:` defines 60/15/10/15
train/calibration/threshold/test proportions. Preserve all translations and detected
duplicates within their component. Report actual counts and every exclusion.

Only 18-scenario choice questions are included. The exact existing descriptions,
choice instruction, utterance, stable option IDs, label-independent per-ID option
permutation and source target are identical between candidates. Require complete
non-truncated rendering in both representations; retain their common eligible
intersection and report attempted/eligible/excluded by language. Require >=200
calibration examples per language and all 18 semantic classes in each held-out
partition. Source scenario labels are not human workflow quality judgments.

The source fields are common; token sequences and contextual ordering differ by
representation. Markers use `choice: <instruction>`, options/markers, then state;
the dual encoder uses the separate instruction/state query and option segments.
This compares complete frozen-base representations and heads, not heads given
identical hidden input. Semantic exports use separate artifact format v2; existing
encoder/pointer artifact v1 retains its exact architecture contract.

## Fixed candidates

- `marker0`: current Laya-derived shared marker head without contextual head layers.
- `marker2`: Laya-derived two-layer contextual head over the full encoder sequence.
- `semantic`: owned separate query/option encoder, attended-token mean pooling,
  two shared 384x384 linear projections initialized to identity with zero biases,
  L2 normalization and fixed cosine-logit multiplier 20. Query text is instruction,
  newline, utterance; every option description is independently encoded. Explicit
  BOS/SEP tokens are attended and included in pooling. Padding never contributes.
  There are no learned weights indexed by scenario ID, option position or language.
- `cosine`: the fixed initial semantic geometry, no optimizer updates.
- `majority`: the source class most frequent in the common training split, ties by
  semantic ID, mapped to each example's provided option IDs. No-advisor always
  abstains; report it without fabricating classification accuracy or model costs.

All candidates use the same original frozen backbone, tokenizer and source rows.
No encoder adaptation. Marker arms share the exact float32 contextual encoder
cache, including all attended token positions, attention lengths and marker
positions; gathered markers alone are insufficient for marker2. Semantic caches
retain independently encoded query/option pooled vectors. Validate both cache
paths against actual production forward on training inputs. Bind all cache bytes,
raw/rendered split hashes, sources, code and environment before fitting.

Train marker0, marker2 and semantic with seeds 17/29/43, primary seed 17 fixed.
For each: exactly five epochs, batch 32, AdamW lr 0.001 / weight_decay 0.01,
clip global gradient norm 1.0, ordinary cross entropy. Each seed uses the same
per-epoch permutation and batch boundaries across arms; no balancing, early
stopping, validation selection or tuning. Randomize the nine run order with
seed 20261020. Identity-initialized semantic parameters are identical across
seeds; the training permutations differ. Report trainable parameter counts,
updates, losses, all runs and any failure. No replacement of a failed seed.

## Calibration, freeze and evaluation

Use the fixed temperature grid (.25,.35,.5,.7,1,1.4,2,3,5,8) on calibration only.
Use threshold .50 through .99 on the separate threshold split, requiring at least
50 accepted examples and empirical error <=5%; prefer largest accepted count,
then larger threshold. This descriptive policy is not a one-sided precision gate.
Convert shuffled option positions to semantic class IDs before class eligibility,
confusion or majority comparison. Freeze every fitted checkpoint and all candidate
and reference policies before test prediction. Open the new test once, retain all
seeds; no further tuning on any opened test.

Report EN/ES attempted/labeled/missing/group/class counts, accuracy, macro recall,
semantic confusions, NLL/Brier/ECE, risk/coverage, accepted counts and errors with
grouped descriptive intervals. Fixed paired cluster bootstrap: 10,000 replicates,
seed 20261020, comparisons to marker2 and majority on identical new test rows.
No universal Laya superiority, causal mechanism or general Braid claim follows.

Prospective stress: reverse all option descriptions/IDs and rerender completely;
keep instruction, utterance and target semantic ID unchanged. Cache the reversed
encoder inputs without head prediction before fitting. After policy freeze, report
reversed accuracy, semantic decision agreement and maximum probability change.
Do not select parameters, thresholds or a favorable model from stress outcomes.

## Resource and stopping envelope

Apple M3 Pro / 36 GiB; CPU float32, 6 threads for fitting, 1 for measured inference.
Inclusive model-study clock <=3 hours starting before prepare; no restart resets
it. Old completed study clocks remain unchanged. RSS <=16 GiB; aggregate task disk
under artifacts/system-one <=16 GiB including the earlier 3.4 GiB. External spend
EUR 0, no provider fallback. Stop on integrity, grouping, resource or feasibility
failure. A negative quality outcome is a valid research result.

Before GO, measure temporary marker2 forward/backward on the first five common
training batches without optimizer steps; discard that temporary head. Use 1.5x
the slowest observed batch time to project all nine five-epoch fits conservatively;
require projection <=90 minutes and total elapsed + projection +30 minutes <=3h.
Bind actual cache bytes, RSS, measured timing and projected budget to registration.
This feasibility probe never optimizes weights or inspects test-head predictions.

Before fitting, retain the actual independent assessment text, a receipt binding
its hash and the exact registration/preparation/cache/feasibility hashes, and a
detached receipt-hash seal. The runner checks their integrity and scope. These
files are bookkeeping, not proof of reviewer identity or operator authorization;
the actual session review and owner direction remain the authority for this run.

After fitting/evaluation stop, export only predeclared seed17 semantic and marker2

select a threshold, establish a confidence bound or predict real native utility.
It does establish that merely filtering these unchanged answers cannot satisfy
both targets on these opened cases. Improving choice accuracy is a necessary
next step here; a new representation or learned policy may change answers, so
this is not a limitation theorem about all future Laya/Braid systems.

### Explanations ruled out or not established

- **Not a missing-checkpoint comparison:** complete original weights were loaded
  strictly by the pinned upstream SDK; no owned head replaced them.
- **Not truncated model input in this run:** all 2,400 audits passed; maximum
  lengths were 179 tokens for multilingual and 213 for typed, within 512.
- **Not newly fitted temperatures:** no new calibration or optimizer steps ran.
- **Not evidence of a general model-size law:** the larger typed model offers no
  dramatic gain here, but this is one task distribution with multiple confounds.
- **Not yet a bilingual construct validation:** EN/ES rendering is mechanically
  consistent with the simulator; human semantic review remains pending.
- **Not a fresh holdout or an independent real workload:** more variants of the
  opened six skeletons cannot repair those boundaries.

## Factors, ordered by decision value

### 1. A decision must have sufficient observable evidence and a supported target

The target is a verified Braid decision, rather than similarity to an intent name
or agreement with a teacher. Distinguish goal, visible facts, observation time,
resource versions, prerequisites, candidate plans and missing observations. If
these are insufficient, the target policy must permit observe/defer/review;
missing evidence must not become a fabricated success or a Boolean false.

This is a construct requirement, not a claim that our 300 cases omit necessary
facts. The external `agent_trace_observability` example inspected earlier shows
why a monitoring summary and teacher votes cannot establish execution success.
Its schema is useful; its labels do not replace an executable verifier.

Laya's browser specialization reports failures caused by inaccessible UI state,
not only classification. Its data recipe uses executed landing pages and adds
mid-task negatives so history alone cannot imply DONE. These are relevant
engineering patterns, with their own domain and observation limits.
[Upstream browser recipe](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/d74e8be46ef5241e4ba2b16cd25e896f24f71373/docs/finetune_browser_agent.md).

**Braid action:** retain the existing typed/verified state and authority boundary;
make supported target families explicit. Audit input sufficiency and legal
candidates before selecting a backbone. Verify that candidate generation includes
an acceptable answer; a ranker cannot recover an option it was never offered.

### 2. Options must be grounded in the context used to score them

Our `SemanticScorer` separately pools instruction/state and option text, then
uses learned normalized projections. A short option such as “Run A then B” is
encoded without A/B's definitions. The marker model and Laya permit joint
attention; however, their current zero-shot results are still poor. Joint
attention is a hypothesis worth isolating, not an obtained solution.

[Sentence-BERT](https://aclanthology.org/D19-1410.pdf), sections 1–3, explains the
separate/joint representation tradeoff for similarity and retrieval. It does not
prove which representation solves workflow state transitions.

The browser recipe reports that making candidates explicit in the option list
improved its own held-out and live evaluations on fixed data. Its truncation
explanation does not transfer to our untruncated run. Candidate grounding and
state-binding can still matter without missing tokens.

**First frozen ablation:** deterministically inline the action definitions already
present in state into each candidate, keeping all facts, option IDs and targets
fixed. Do not supply executed final states, hidden validity, traces or gold.
Re-audit complete token budgets, compare unchanged checkpoints and record all
failures. Treat this as development on opened cases, not a new confirmatory test.

### 3. Supervision must break shortcuts and cover compositional structure

Our useful MASSIVE intent scores concern a different task. The frozen encoder
features and heads trained on source-taxonomy decisions are not task-adapted
workflow reasoning. Original Laya weights also do not acquire that specialization
merely by being loaded correctly.

[HANS](https://aclanthology.org/P19-1334.pdf) constructs cases that defeat lexical,
subsequence and constituent shortcuts in NLI. It motivates deliberately confusing
positive/negative pairs rather than more easy paraphrases.
[Contrast Sets](https://aclanthology.org/2020.findings-emnlp.117.pdf) evaluates local
meaning changes across ten NLP datasets. Transfer to Braid requires our own
correct constructs; contrastive wording alone is not a proof of coverage.

For synthetic data, vary causal compositions, goal structures, observation gaps,
constraint interactions and sequence length. Keep paired labels executable and
preserve all valid ties. Balance nuisance cues such as IDs, wording, history
length and defer frequency independently of the target. More random seeds or
names within one skeleton do not provide new structural coverage.

[Yao and Koller (NAACL 2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.naacl-long.25.pdf) find
that structural augmentation distribution matters, with a uniform grammar useful
on their compositional datasets. Their Table 9 also shows incorrect generated
surface forms. Use program-first generation and round-trip/semantic review;
a valid program does not automatically make its EN/ES description faithful.

[APIGen](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.18518v1), sections 3.2 and 5, separates
format checks, actual execution checks and model-based semantic checks. Its
ablation adds rejected execution/semantic data back and reports worse function
calling. [ToolACE](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.00920v1), sections 2.3 and 5.3,
also ablates rule/model verification and diversity. These provide more directly
relevant data-quality evidence than similarity benchmarks, but their function-call
benchmarks do not establish Braid workflow reliability. Their semantic judge is
still a model; passing it is not a proof or a substitute for our human admission.
Borrow the layered checking pattern using owned offline functions and verified
outcomes, without executing arbitrary public APIs or inheriting teacher truth.

The [official FunctionGemma model card](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/functiongemma/model_card)
likewise positions a compact tool model as a base for task-specific adaptation.
This is contemporary practitioner evidence for specialization, not a recommendation
to add another checkpoint to our opened test. No Gemma license was accepted,
weights acquired or performance measured here.

**Future fitting prerequisite:** source and human admission, disjoint grouped
train/development/calibration/threshold/test, and a small capacity check on an
approved development set. A model unable to learn those distinctions should not
trigger an expensive scale-up. No training is authorized by this report.

### 4. Choice-order robustness must be measured and designed

Normal/reversed agreement is only 50–63% for the original models in English,
and 46–56% in Spanish. Do not mistake stable wrong answers for understanding.

Laya's sequential encoder positions let listing order change representations.
`parallel_layout` resets option positions and masks cross-option attention, with
a head that has no positional encoding. The source explicitly treats layout as a
property of the trained weights; published checkpoints default to sequential.
It also requires a newer backend interface. Do not flip the flag on frozen
weights and call it a faithful reproduction.
[Source](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/d74e8be46ef5241e4ba2b16cd25e896f24f71373/laya/common.py#L282).

[Zheng et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2309.03882v3), sections 2–3, diagnose option-ID
bias in decoder LLMs and study permutation debiasing. Their token-generation
mechanism is not a demonstrated explanation for our bidirectional marker scorer.
It supports testing, not copying their correction unchanged.

**Experiments:** separate position permutations from ID renaming and description
changes. Full averaging over all 24 permutations of four choices is an
inference-only equivariance reference with a large cost multiplier, not a promised
latency win. Two-order agreement does not certify all permutations. A candidate-wise
joint scorer or a newly trained parallel layout is a later architectural control.
Ordinal score levels keep their semantic order; do not shuffle them like choices.

### 5. Reliability requires valid selection and risk evidence, not a confident field

[Laya's act-head diagnostic](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/d74e8be46ef5241e4ba2b16cd25e896f24f71373/research/evals/act_head_eval.py)
explicitly states that released action heads were not trained to provide useful
act decisions. The current fine-tuner's `_forward` discards `_act`; its loss
optimizes answer logits. Our post-hoc constant scores corroborate the practical
limitation on this pilot. `act_probability` is neither permission nor a risk bound.

The source distinguishes entropy-based `confidence` from max-probability
`answer_confidence`. It also fits abstention cuts using empirical accepted error,
with a pseudo-error margin; it expressly disclaims a formal coverage guarantee.
Missing option-count buckets fall to default 0 if no default is supplied.
[Calibration source](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/d74e8be46ef5241e4ba2b16cd25e896f24f71373/laya/calibrate.py#L411),
[gate source](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/d74e8be46ef5241e4ba2b16cd25e896f24f71373/laya/confidence.py#L190).
Native Braid must retain refusal for unadmitted combinations and its independent
authority checks; copying Laya must not weaken them.

[Guo et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/guo17a/guo17a.pdf), section 4.2:
a positive scalar temperature preserves argmax, so it cannot fix top-1 choices.
[Ovadia et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/1906.02530v2), sections 4–5: calibration on
IID validation does not assure calibration under shift. Neither result means
calibration is useless; it has a different objective from decision accuracy.

[Selective Classification](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/file/4a8423d5e91fda00bb7e46540e2b0cf1-Paper.pdf)
and [Learn then Test](https://arxiv.org/html/2110.01052v5), section 3.2, support
risk/coverage selection with finite-sample and multiplicity treatment under their
sampling assumptions. LTT explicitly assumes IID calibration examples.
[Conformal Risk Control](https://arxiv.org/html/2208.02814v4) controls expected
monotone loss; that does not automatically establish the accepted conditional
error or a high-probability bound required by our protocol.
[Non-exchangeable CRC](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.01262v2), theorem 1, adds a
distribution-gap term. Unknown drift cannot be erased by calling a method conformal.

**Already implemented, not a new feature request:** Braid's reliability protocol
requires at most 1% accepted error and at least 50% coverage, with family alpha
0.05 across 12 cells (three types × two domains × EN/ES). Its exact one-sided
zero-error calculation gives 546 independent accepted primary observations per
cell. That condition is necessary only for that zero-error calculation, not a
promise of acceptance; observed errors, dependence and unresolved labels matter.
The current one-lineage pilot cannot satisfy the sampling requirement by counting
translations or repetitions. Strict native requests currently abstain before
loading experimental models. Zero accepted coverage is safe refusal, not useful
learned reliability.

### 6. Teachers, negatives and fallback must earn their role

Current frozen Laya is not an adequate automatic truth source for these simulator
labels. Keep exact oracle outcomes over teacher disagreements. A teacher should
first beat development references and retain that advantage on the states it labels.

[RocketQA](https://aclanthology.org/2021.naacl-main.466.pdf), Table 3 and section
4.2, shows that hard negatives without denoising can worsen retrieval, while
verified/filtered negatives help in that setup. This supports checking proposed
negatives and valid ties; it does not make a teacher infallible or transfer its
retrieval gains to Braid.

[DAgger](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v15/ross11a/ross11a.pdf), sections 2–3,
addresses the policy-induced state distribution and compounding errors with an
expert supervisor. Its lesson is to include states actually visited by the policy
and obtain reliable corrections. Calling a larger local LLM is not equivalent to
having that expert. The browser recipe itself reports a worse large-model fallback
on its task. Measure fallback correctness and complete latency before adopting it.

A production hybrid can use legitimate runtime verifiers/constraints to exclude
unsupported candidates and retain escalation. Keep such a verifier-assisted arm
separate from neural semantic accuracy; never feed the custodian simulator oracle
back into model inputs and report the result as improved comprehension.

### 7. General typed decisions require separate type and language constructs

Choice is the only primitive measured in this pilot. Boolean questions need
polarity/label controls and explicit unknown handling outside true/false. Ordinal
score questions need defined levels, ordered metrics and asymmetric costs where
underestimating risk matters. Expected severity is not confidence in correctness.
The Laya README documents Boolean-label and ordinal-position weaknesses; those
reports motivate controls, not new measured claims about our models.
[Known limitations](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/d74e8be46ef5241e4ba2b16cd25e896f24f71373/README.md#L1659).

[XNLI](https://aclanthology.org/D18-1269.pdf) provides a cross-lingual understanding
benchmark, not a workflow planner. Use EN/ES meaning-preserving and meaning-flipping
pairs, native Spanish wording and independent semantic review; do not infer Spanish
reliability from an English checkpoint or translation consistency alone.

### 8. Isolate causes before changing loss, model size or scale

The upstream three-seed CE/RLCD comparison reports nearly equal mean accuracy,
with different variance. It does not support a guaranteed large gain from RLCD
or replacing it with CE.
[Upstream comparison](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/pull/1012).
[Accounting for Variance](https://arxiv.org/html/2103.03098v1) treats data sampling,
initialization and optimization choices as material sources of benchmarking
uncertainty. Three seeds are a useful engineering check, not independent native
sources or a universal sufficient sample size.

A matched future study should hold data, backbone and budget fixed while changing
one factor, then test interactions only when useful. Distinguish head-only fitting
from encoder adaptation: our previous cached-feature head experiment did not
fine-tune the encoder, whereas Laya's default specialization can do so. Observed
model differences currently confound this with width, pretraining and domain.
